tasks.short: Read work documents to determine required tower work

steps.what: Read work orders, blueprints, plans, datasheets and site drawings to determine required work

tasks.design: Keep scope interpretation with the technician using source records in {DOCS} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. A generated summary does not establish that current drawings, constraints and conflicting instructions have been understood.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work scope depends on current technical documents and site conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing work orders and document access support preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Identify conflicts, missing detail and the implications for physical work.
tasks.human_edge: Connect written instructions to the actual site and equipment.
tasks.altitude: Own technical understanding before work begins.

evidence.claim: Technical reading and scope judgement retain full time here; no separate repeated retrieval burden is established.

assumptions: The baseline is understanding the work, without inventing a document-indexing process.
Document owners supply work orders and drawings; technician clarification remains in s1.
No new automation service means no extra upkeep.
research_questions: Is locating the current document a measurable burden separate from understanding it?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Scope interpretation remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Complete project status, progress and work-detail reports

steps.what: Capture project status, progress and work details against the correct work order
Populate reports with recorded status, progress and linked work details
Check reports for missing work details and complete the internal project record

tasks.design: Configure native report layouts in {OPS_SYSTEM} to assemble captured entries into {DOCS}. Retain observation, progress assessment, correction and completion with the technician; no automatic completion or safety certification is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work details may be copied from job records into a separate status report.
tasks.enabler_now: Field service systems hold work-order information and support recap or reporting capabilities.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish actual progress from assumptions and explain unresolved work.
tasks.human_edge: Verify what happened at the site and communicate limitations.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time copying work details and more time checking project truth.

evidence.claim: Dynamics 365 Field Service with Copilot writes work-order recaps for managers; this supports record reuse, not the exact deterministic design or a measured saving.
Native report population and the proposed time effect are unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: In s1 the technician captures project ID, work-order ID, reporting date, completed activities, remaining activities, hours, blockers and evidence links; its 40 hours includes observation and status clarification.
Crew members supply factual updates; two added other-role hours cover clarification of missing entries rather than assuming free structured progress.
Missing or conflicting entries return to manual correction in s3; no inferred sold-out, completion or safety flag is used.
Try existing OPS_SYSTEM reporting before a custom generator; report completion stays internal and is not a customer acceptance signature.
Seven additional focal hours cover layout maintenance and reconciliation checks; already generated reports earn no new saving.
research_questions: Does native reporting remove duplicate report preparation after capture and correction time?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65; gross 35 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 28. E1 range 0-20 allows existing reports and incomplete site updates.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take digital site-survey and completed-work photos

steps.what: Take site survey photos or photos of work performed using digital cameras

tasks.design: Retain on-site image capture with the technician using {OTHER}, a digital camera or camera-equipped work device. Automatic filing could support later reporting, but this task does not establish a separate filing baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful evidence requires the right physical view, context and image quality.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing digital cameras capture images directly.
tasks.still_hard: Choose views that show the site or work accurately.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise what needs documenting and obtain a clear image.
tasks.altitude: Own useful visual evidence of the site and work.

evidence.claim: On-site photography remains physical work; digital storage does not establish reduced capture time.

assumptions: OTHER denotes a digital camera or camera-equipped work device.
Image selection, framing and quality checks remain in s1; reporting uses these existing images without claiming their capture as saved.
No new automation or maintenance is added.
research_questions: Is repeated image filing a separate measured burden outside capture?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Physical image capture and quality checking remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Locate tower work sites with mapping software

steps.what: Check tower site identifiers, coordinates and work-order location details
Open the mapping software at the checked tower site coordinates
outputs: mapped tower location with source identifier

steps.what: Locate the tower site and resolve discrepancies between map, access point and work order
inputs: mapped tower location with source identifier

tasks.design: Configure a native map link from {OPS_SYSTEM} to {OTHER}, the mapping application. Retain site identity, access-point and discrepancy checks with the technician; a map pin is not proof of safe or authorised access.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordinates or site addresses may be repeatedly copied into a separate map search.
tasks.enabler_now: Mapping applications accept explicit coordinate links.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve incorrect coordinates, similar site names and access differences.
tasks.human_edge: Confirm the intended site against work instructions.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated location entry while retaining site verification.

evidence.claim: Explicit coordinate links can open a map without repeated typing; the exact design and savings are model knowledge.

assumptions: OTHER denotes the mapping application; use native work-order map links before custom integrations.

The site owner supplies site ID, latitude, longitude, coordinate reference and record revision; in s1 the technician captures and verifies these against the work order, including clarification within its 25 hours.
Two added other-role hours cover site-coordinator corrections; there is no free structured address producer.
Missing or inconsistent coordinates require manual lookup and confirmation in s3; no unattended routing or access decision follows.
Five added focal hours cover link validation and location-format upkeep; existing map links earn no new saving.
research_questions: Do native map links remove re-entry after coordinate verification and correction costs?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70; gross 30 minus 5 focal upkeep gives central net 25. E1 range 0-15 allows existing map links and poor location data; travel and physical access receive no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated report and location entry while retaining site and technical judgement.
reach: Resolve work scope with site engineers
role.ambitious_version: A tower technician who reuses checked work records and map coordinates while retaining technical reading, photography and site verification.
